basis: Defining immunodeficiency and cholangitis; enteric infection 4/4 with chronic diarrhea 2/4; bronchiectasis 2/5 establishes pulmonary damage. Otitis evidence limited and omitted under cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: enteric infections affect 4/4 and chronic diarrhea 2/4; intestinal disease is a common manifestation rather than the syndrome's defining hepatobiliary lesion.

basis: Palmoplantar keratoderma and esophageal neoplasia explicitly define the syndrome; esophageal neoplasm HPO frequency 80-99%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: esophageal neoplasia is an explicit defining component with HPO frequency 80-99%; oral leukoplakia provides additional gastrointestinal evidence.

basis: Intestinal atresia and ulceration eroding umbilical vessels with severe hemorrhage define the syndrome; hemorrhagic anemia occurs in 80-99%. Cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: defining umbilical cord ulceration erodes fetal vessels and causes severe intrauterine hemorrhage; additional cardiac and arterial malformations occur in 30-79%.

basis: Malignant lymphoid cells establish the haematologic axis; lymphoma requires infectious_immune. Testicular origin does not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymphoma is a malignancy of lymphoid blood cells, including when confined to an extranodal site; marrow involvement is not required.

basis: Hypocellular marrow failure defines aplastic anemia; immune-mediated stem-cell destruction accounts for most cases, approximately 70-80%. Inherited and toxic forms also occur.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most cases, approximately 70-80%, involve immune-mediated marrow destruction; the umbrella rule concerns the usual disease rather than requiring every subtype to share its mechanism.

basis: Mineral metabolism disorder causes arterial stenosis; rickets/osteomalacia and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%. Renal and hepatic calcification lack established functional injury.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis occurs in 30-79%, but the supplied evidence does not establish impaired renal function or damaging renal deposition.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment represents functional loss and occurs in 30-79%; occasional frequencies for individual hearing-loss subtypes do not negate the aggregate frequency.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining neurodegeneration; hearing impairment affects 27/73 (~37%). Diarrhea in 59/72 alone does not establish intestinal injury; skeletal damage frequency is uncertain.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea affects 59/72 (~82%), but the evidence does not establish direct intestinal injury or persistent intestinal loss of function rather than a symptom.

basis: Antibody-mediated demyelination defines the disease; optic neuritis is explicitly a core diagnostic presentation and directly damages the optic nerve, assigned to ocular.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic neuritis is explicitly a core demyelinating event in the diagnostic definition; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.

basis: Jeune thoracic dysplasia has defining short ribs, thoracic constriction and pulmonary hypoplasia/restrictive respiratory dysfunction. Renal damage is not established for this subtype.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive respiratory dysfunction are defining features of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy; renal ancestry alone supplies no additional organ label.

basis: Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal habitus are explicit defining features. Psychiatric manifestations have no axis; facial dysmorphism does not establish further organ disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: marfanoid skeletal habitus is an explicit component of the syndrome's definition; primary structural skeletal abnormalities need not establish additional functional loss.
